meaning: traffic; transport (how easy it is to get around)

senses.en: traffic: the flow of cars and people on the roads
transport links; getting around a place (交通方便 'well connected')

examples.en: Is it easy to get around where you live?
examples.analysis: 交通 is the subject and 方便 'convenient' describes it: 交通方便 is the set way to say a place has good transport links. 你家那边 'over where your home is' sets the place first as the topic. 吗 turns it into a yes/no question.

examples.zh: 这儿交通不太方便，没有地铁。
examples.en: It's not easy to get around here. There's no subway.
examples.analysis: Here 交通 means transport links, not traffic jams: 交通不太方便 'transport isn't very convenient', and 没有地铁 'there's no subway' explains why. 不太 + adjective softens the complaint to 'not very'.

examples.zh: 早上交通不好，路上车很多，我们早一点儿出门吧。
examples.en: Traffic is bad in the mornings, with lots of cars on the road, so let's leave a bit earlier.
examples.analysis: Here 交通 is the traffic itself: 交通不好 'the traffic is bad', and 路上车很多 'lots of cars on the road' says why; on its own, 交通不好 could also mean poor transport links. 早上 sets the time. 早一点儿 'a bit earlier' goes before 出门 'head out', and 吧 makes it a suggestion.

collocations.en: well connected; easy to get around

meaning: to take a shower or a bath

senses.en: to take a shower; to have a bath (washing the whole body)
to bathe someone: 给孩子洗澡 'give the child a bath'

examples.en: I'll shower first, then eat.
examples.analysis: 洗澡 is a complete verb phrase, 'take a shower', and needs no object. 先… 然后… 'first…, then…' orders the two actions. 洗澡 covers both a shower and a bath; at home in China it most often means a shower.

examples.en: Hurry up and go take your shower!
examples.analysis: A request with no subject, as when a parent hurries a child. 快点儿 'quicker' goes before the verb, and 去 + 洗澡 means 'go and shower'. 洗澡 is a separable verb: words can go between its halves, as in 洗个澡 'take a shower' or 洗完澡 'after showering'.

examples.en: I'm too tired today. I'm skipping my shower.
examples.analysis: 不 + 洗澡 + 了 marks a change of plan: 'not showering after all'. Without the final 了, 不洗澡 would simply state a habit or a refusal. 太累了 'too tired' comes first and gives the reason.

meaning: road; highway (a public road between towns)

senses.en: road or highway linking towns and cities, as opposed to a city street
in 高速公路: expressway; motorway

examples.en: Does this road go to Beijing?
examples.analysis: 这 + 条 + 公路: long, narrow things such as roads and rivers take the measure word 条. 能到北京 'can reach Beijing' asks where the road leads. Inside a city people say 路 or 马路; 公路 suggests a road out of town.

examples.zh: 公路上车很多，开慢一点儿。
examples.en: There's a lot of traffic on the road. Drive a bit slower.
examples.analysis: 公路 + 上 'on the road': a noun + 上 means 'on' it. 车很多 'cars are many' is how Chinese says 'there's a lot of traffic'. In 开慢一点儿 the adjective follows the verb: 'drive slower', a request with no subject.

examples.zh: 那儿没有公路，只能坐船去。
examples.en: There's no road out there. You can only get there by boat.
examples.analysis: 没有 + 公路 says there is no proper road there. 只能 'can only' + 坐船去 'go by boat': the means of travel (坐船) comes before the verb 去. This is 公路 as a road linking places, not a street.

senses.en: head of a school: principal; headmaster
head of a university: president
as a title after a surname: 王校长 'Principal Wang'

measure.note: 一位校长 (polite); 个 in casual talk

examples.en: Have you met the new principal?
examples.analysis: 见过 'have seen or met before' asks about experience: 过 after the verb marks it. 新 'new' goes straight before 校长 with no 的, as one-syllable adjectives usually do. 吗 makes it a yes/no question.

examples.en: The principal's looking for you. You'd better go now.
examples.analysis: 校长 is the subject: 校长 + 找 + 你. 找 + a person means 'want to see someone', like English 'is looking for you'. 快去吧 'go quickly' urges the listener, and 吧 softens the order into advice.

examples.zh: 校长今天不在，明天再来吧。
examples.en: The principal isn't in today. Come back tomorrow.
examples.analysis: 不在 'not in' says the person is away, with no place word needed. 明天再来 'come again tomorrow': 再 marks a repeat that is still to come. Inside a school, 校长 alone works like a name, since everyone knows who is meant.

related.en: head of a hospital or a college

hook: 长 read zhǎng means 'head; chief', as in 班长 'class monitor' and 市长 'mayor': 校 'school' + 长 'head'.

senses.en: a bad person; someone who means harm
the bad guy; the villain (in a film or a story)

examples.en: Don't be scared. He's not a bad guy.
examples.analysis: 坏人 is the object of 是: 他不是坏人 'he isn't a bad person', with 不 before 是 to negate it. 别怕 'don't be afraid' uses 别, the spoken 'don't'. A line to reassure a child or a nervous friend.

examples.en: Who's the bad guy in the movie?
examples.analysis: 电影里 'in the film' sets the scene first. 谁 'who' stays where the answer would go: 谁是坏人? / 他是坏人. 坏人 here is the villain of a story, the everyday word for 'the bad guy'.

examples.zh: 那儿晚上有坏人，别一个人去。
examples.en: There are bad people around there at night. Don't go alone.
examples.analysis: 有 + 坏人 'there are bad people': 有 says something exists, and 那儿 'there' and 晚上 'at night' give the place and time. In 别一个人去, 一个人 'one person' before the verb means 'by yourself'.

collocations.en: play the bad guy (be the strict one)

meaning: level; standard (of skill, quality or living)

senses.en: level of skill or ability (in a language, of a doctor, a player)
standard; level of quality (生活水平 'standard of living')

examples.en: Your Chinese is really good!
examples.analysis: Chinese rates 水平 as high or low: 水平高 means 'good', 水平不高 'not very good'. 你 is the topic and 汉语水平 'Chinese level' the subject: 你汉语水平 is 'as for you, your Chinese level', with no 的, which is common in speech. 真 'really' makes it an exclamation of praise.

examples.zh: 我的水平还不够，要多练习。
examples.en: I'm not good enough yet. I need more practice.
examples.analysis: 水平 + 不够 'my level isn't enough' is a modest way to say 'not good enough'. 还 'still' adds the 'yet'. 多 + verb (多练习) means 'do more of it', the usual way to say 'practice more'.

examples.zh: 这儿的医生水平怎么样？
examples.en: How good are the doctors here?
examples.analysis: 医生水平 'the doctors' level' asks about their skill, as when choosing a hospital. 怎么样 'how is it?' sits at the end, where the answer goes: 水平很高 'very good'. 这儿的 'of this place' comes before the noun.

collocations.en: skilled; impressive (a person or their work)

senses.en: advanced; at a higher level (a class, a course)
high-end; upscale; fancy (a hotel, a bag, a restaurant)
senior in rank: 高级经理 'senior manager'

examples.en: Your bag looks so fancy!
examples.analysis: 高级 is the predicate, with 真 'really' before it and no 是: Chinese adjectives work like verbs here. 高级 in this sense means high-end, said of things that look expensive or top quality.

examples.zh: 不用去太高级的饭馆，便宜一点儿的就行。
examples.en: No need to go anywhere too fancy. Somewhere cheaper is fine.
examples.analysis: 太高级 + 的 + 饭馆 'too fancy a restaurant': with an adverb like 太 in front, the description needs 的 before the noun. 不用 'no need to' + 去. 便宜一点儿的 'a slightly cheaper one' drops the noun, and 就行 means 'will do'.

examples.zh: 高级班太难了，我还是上中级班吧。
examples.en: The advanced class is too hard. I think I'll take the intermediate one.
examples.analysis: 高级 goes straight before 班 'class' with no 的, as with other fixed levels: 中级 'intermediate', 高级 'advanced'. 还是…吧 'I'd better…' settles on the second choice. 上 + class means 'attend'.

senses.en: homework; a school or course assignment
(formal, at work) task; operation, as on a work site

measure.note: 一个作业 'an assignment'; 很多作业 'a lot of homework'

examples.en: Have you finished your homework?
examples.analysis: 作业 comes right after 你 as the topic, then 写完了 'finished writing': the thing talked about goes first. 完 after the verb marks completion, and 了吗 asks whether it has happened. 写作业 and 做作业 both mean 'do homework'.

examples.en: Homework first, then TV.
examples.analysis: 做作业 'do homework' is verb + object. 先… 再… 'first…, then…' sets the order, the classic rule at home. With no subject, it reads as an instruction to a child.

examples.en: The teacher didn't give any homework today.
examples.analysis: 留作业 'leave homework' is how teachers set it. 没 + verb says it did not happen, so the verb takes no completion 了 (not 没留了作业). Without a number, 作业 works like English 'homework': no measure word and no plural.

senses.en: to achieve; to gain (results, success, progress): 取得好成绩
(formal) to obtain (a qualification, someone's agreement)

examples.en: Our team came first!
examples.analysis: 取得 + 了 + 第一名 'gained first place': 了 marks the result as achieved. 取得 sounds a little formal, like a news report or a speech; in casual talk people often say 得了第一名. 我们队 'our team' needs no 的.

examples.en: What does it take to get good grades?
examples.analysis: 取得 + 好成绩 'achieve good results' is the classic pairing: 取得 takes results won through effort as its object. 怎么才能 'how can one manage to…', with 才 'only then', asks what it takes.

examples.zh: 他很努力，可是没取得好成绩。
examples.en: He worked really hard, but he didn't get good results.
examples.analysis: 没 + 取得 says the result did not come, so no completion 了 follows the verb (a sentence-final 了 can still appear, as in 好久没来了). 可是 'but' sets the effort against the outcome. 取得 suits results earned by effort, which is why it follows 努力 'hard-working' so naturally.

meaning: cooked; ripe; familiar with (a person or a place)

senses.en: cooked through; done (food); ripe (fruit)
familiar; knowing someone or somewhere well: 跟他很熟, 对这儿不熟
(of sleep) deep: 睡熟了 'fast asleep'

examples.en: The dumplings are ready. Come and eat!
examples.analysis: 熟 + 了 'cooked now': 了 marks the change from raw to done. Like other adjectives, 熟 needs no 是. In casual speech, especially in the north, you will also hear it read shóu.

examples.en: Do you know this area well?
examples.analysis: 对 + place + 熟 'familiar with a place': 对 introduces what you know. 吗 makes it a yes/no question; the reply is 熟 or 不太熟. 这儿 'here' means the whole neighborhood, not only this spot.

examples.en: I don't know him that well.
examples.analysis: 跟 + person + 熟 'familiar with someone'. 不太熟 'not that familiar' means you know the person a little but are not close. Compare 不认识, 'not acquainted at all'.

collocations.en: be familiar with (a place, a job)

related.en: to know; to be acquainted with

senses.en: seat (on a bus, train or plane; in a theater, classroom or restaurant)
an assigned, numbered seat: 座位号 'seat number'

examples.en: Is this seat taken?
examples.analysis: The standard line before sitting down, literally 'does this seat have someone?'. 这 + 个 + 座位 uses the measure word 个. 有人 'someone's there' means taken; the reply is 有人 'taken' or 没人 'free'.

examples.en: There are no seats left on the bus.
examples.analysis: 没有 + 座位 + 了: 了 marks a change, 'no seats now', which English says with 'left'. 车上 'on the bus' sets the place. Without 了 the sentence would state the fact with no sense of change.

examples.zh: 这儿太热了，我们换个座位吧。
examples.en: It's too hot here. Let's sit somewhere else.
examples.analysis: 换 + 个 + 座位 'change to another seat': 个 stands for 一个, with 一 dropped, as often in speech. 吧 turns the plan into a suggestion. 太热了 'too hot' gives the reason first.

related.en: seat (as in 座位, 让座); also a measure word for buildings, mountains, bridges

senses.en: green, the color: 绿色的衣服 'green clothes'
green: eco-friendly (绿色出行 'green travel'); 绿色食品 is officially certified safe, low-pollution food

examples.zh: 这件绿色的衣服挺好看的。
examples.en: This green piece of clothing looks pretty nice.
examples.analysis: 绿色 + 的 + 衣服: the color word describes the noun through 的. 这 + 件 + 衣服: 件 is the measure word for 衣服 and for tops and coats (trousers and skirts take 条). 挺…的 'quite, pretty' is a soft spoken compliment.

examples.zh: 我不喜欢绿色，有别的颜色吗？
examples.en: I don't like green. Do you have any other colors?
examples.analysis: Here 绿色 is a noun on its own, the object of 喜欢: 'I don't like green'. 有别的颜色吗 'are there other colors?' is the shop line. The 色 in 绿色 is the same 色 'color' as in 颜色.

examples.en: The green one is mine.
examples.analysis: 绿色的那个 'that green one': color + 的 before 那个, with the noun dropped because both people can see it. 是我的 'is mine': 我的 also stands on its own. Useful at a coat rack or a baggage belt.

senses.en: white, the color: 白色的车 'a white car'
on its own, the color white: 我喜欢白色 'I like white'

examples.zh: 我要白色的，不要黑色的。
examples.en: I want the white one, not the black one.
examples.analysis: 白色的 'the white one': color + 的 with the noun left out. 要 'want' and 不要 'don't want' set the two choices side by side, a quick way to pick in a shop.

examples.en: Is your car white?
examples.analysis: 是 + 白色 + 的 'is a white one' says what color something is. With color words ending in 色, Chinese usually uses this 是…的 frame; 很白 instead means 'very white' or 'fair'. 吗 makes it a yes/no question.

examples.en: Don't buy the white one. It's hard to get clean.
examples.analysis: 别 + 买 'don't buy' is a friendly warning. 白色的 again stands for 'a white one' without naming the thing. 很难洗 'very hard to wash' gives the reason: 难 + verb means 'hard to do'.

meaning: in one's heart or mind (在我心中: 'to me')

senses.en: in one's heart; in one's mind: 在我心中 'to me; in my heart'
X心中的Y: the Y someone imagines or holds dear (我心中的北京)

examples.zh: 她是我心中最好的老师。
examples.en: To me, she's the best teacher there is.
examples.analysis: 我心中 'in my heart' limits the claim to the speaker's own feeling: 最好的老师 is 'the best' in my eyes. 心中 is a little more literary than everyday 心里, so it suits praise, speeches and songs.

examples.en: Who matters most to you?
examples.analysis: 在 + 你心中 'in your heart' frames the question at the start. 谁 'who' sits where the answer would go: 我妈妈最重要. A heart-to-heart question; 在你心里 is the more casual version.

examples.zh: 我心中的北京不是这样的。
examples.en: This isn't the Beijing I had in mind.
examples.analysis: 我心中的北京 'the Beijing in my mind' is the picture the speaker carries of the city, whether imagined or remembered; 的 joins 我心中 to 北京. 不是这样的 'isn't like this' sets that picture against what is in front of them.

collocations.en: have a clear idea of where things stand

related.en: in one's heart or mind (more everyday)

senses.en: old friend; someone you have known for a long time
(slang, euphemism) a woman's period: 老朋友来了

measure.note: 一位老朋友 (polite); 个 in casual talk

examples.zh: 他是我的老朋友，人很好。
examples.en: He's an old friend of mine. He's a really nice guy.
examples.analysis: 老朋友 is one word: 老 here means 'of long standing', not 'old in age'. 我的老朋友 'an old friend of mine'. 人很好 'very nice as a person' is the common way to vouch for someone.

examples.en: My old friend! It's been ages since you came by!
examples.analysis: 老朋友 is used here to address someone, like 'my old friend!'. 好久没来了 'haven't come for ages': 好久 'a long time' + 没 + verb + 了 says something has not happened for a while, up to now.

examples.zh: 我们不是老朋友，昨天才认识的。
examples.en: We're not old friends. We only met yesterday.
examples.analysis: 不是老朋友 'not old friends'. 才 'only, as late as' stresses how recent it is: 昨天才认识 'got to know each other only yesterday'. The final 的 puts the focus on when it happened.

senses.en: (after a verb) not long; only a short time: 刚来不久 'only just arrived'
soon; before long; shortly after: 不久就…, 不久以后

examples.en: You two haven't known each other long, have you?
examples.analysis: Verb + 不久 says only a short time has passed since it happened: 认识不久 'have known each other a short time'. 吧 at the end makes a guess you expect the listener to confirm, like English '…, have you?'.

examples.zh: 他到北京不久就找到了工作。
examples.en: Not long after he got to Beijing, he found a job.
examples.analysis: Event + 不久 + 就 + next event: 'not long after A, B happened'. 就 stresses how soon B followed. In 找到了, 到 shows the search succeeded and 了 that it is done.

examples.zh: 不久以后，这儿会有地铁。
examples.en: Before long, there'll be a subway here.
examples.analysis: 不久以后 'before long' at the start sets the time; with 会 + 有 'will have' it points to the near future (about a past event it would mean 'not long afterwards'). 不久 sounds a bit more like storytelling or news than 很快 'soon', which is common in casual talk.

related.en: right away; at once (much sooner than 不久 'before long')

meaning: cheap; inexpensive; (noun) a small unfair gain

senses.en: cheap; inexpensive; low-priced
a small advantage gained at someone else's cost: 占便宜 'take advantage'

examples.en: Can you make it a little cheaper?
examples.analysis: The basic bargaining line. 便宜 + 一点儿 'a bit cheaper': 'a bit more X' is simply adjective + 一点儿. 能…吗 'can you…?' keeps it polite. The second syllable of 便宜 is neutral: piányi.

examples.en: Cheap doesn't always mean good.
examples.analysis: 便宜的 'cheap things': adjective + 的 stands for the things themselves, so 便宜的 is the subject. 不一定 'not necessarily' keeps the claim modest. A common thing to say while shopping.

examples.en: He's always taking advantage of people.
examples.analysis: Here 便宜 is a noun, 'a small gain at others' expense', and the object of 占 'take': 占别人的便宜 'take advantage of others'. 老是 'always' often signals annoyance. The reading stays piányi.

related.en: convenient: the same 便, read biàn

senses.en: parking lot; car park (open-air or in a building)

examples.en: Is there a parking lot here?
examples.analysis: 有 + 停车场 asks whether something exists at a place, with 这儿 'here' first. The word is 停车 'park a car' + 场 'a large open space', the 场 of 机场 'airport'. The reply is 有 or 没有.

examples.en: I'll wait for you in the parking lot.
examples.analysis: 在 + 停车场 + 等你: the place with 在 comes before the verb, not after it as in English. With no time word, the context gives the future 'I'll wait'.

examples.zh: 医院的停车场满了，坐地铁去吧。
examples.en: The hospital parking lot is full. Let's take the subway.
examples.analysis: 停车场 + 满了 'is full now': 了 marks the new situation. 医院的 'the hospital's' comes before the noun. 坐地铁去 'go by subway' puts the transport before 去, and 吧 makes it a suggestion.

meaning: a large amount of; a great deal of; large numbers of

senses.en: a large amount of; lots of (before a noun: 大量的水, 大量时间)
in large numbers; in bulk (before a verb, mostly written)

examples.zh: 运动以后，别一次喝大量的水。
examples.en: After exercise, don't drink a lot of water all at once.
examples.analysis: 大量 + 的 + 水 'a large amount of water': here the amount itself is the point, and 一次 'in one go' sharpens it. 大量 only goes before a noun or a verb; unlike 多, it cannot be the predicate (no 水很大量). In casual talk people also say 别一次喝太多水.

examples.zh: 夏天有大量的游客来这儿。
examples.en: In summer, huge numbers of tourists come here.
examples.analysis: 有 + 大量的游客 + 来这儿: 有 introduces the group, then the sentence says what they do. 大量 works for things you can count, such as tourists, as well as for amounts like water.

examples.zh: 这个工作要花大量的时间。
examples.en: This job takes a huge amount of time.
examples.analysis: 要花 'will need to spend' + 大量的时间: here 要 means 'requires', not 'want'. 花 is the usual verb for spending time. 大量的时间 sounds a bit like a report; in chat you might hear 要花很多时间. 这个工作 'this job' is the topic.

related.en: many; much (can be the predicate: 人很多)

meaning: to take up (space, time); to hold or occupy (a place)

senses.en: to take up (space or time): 占地方 'take up room'
to save, hold or occupy a place: 占座位 'save a seat'
to take (a gain or advantage, often at someone's cost): 占便宜 'take advantage'

examples.en: Could you save me a seat?
examples.analysis: 占 + 个 + 座位 'hold a seat': 占 means claiming a place before others take it. 帮我 + verb 'do it for me' frames the favor, and 好吗 'OK?' at the end softens the request. 占座 is the short form.

examples.zh: 工作占了我大部分时间。
examples.en: Work takes up most of my time.
examples.analysis: 占 + time 'take up time': the subject 工作 is what uses it up. 了 shows this has happened so far. 我大部分时间 'most of my time' needs no 的.

examples.en: This bag is small. It doesn't take up much room.
examples.analysis: 不 + 占 + 地方 'doesn't take up space': 地方 'place, room' is the object. 不占地方 is a stock phrase for compact things; the opposite is 很占地方 'takes up a lot of room'. 很小 gives the reason first.

related.en: (in 占便宜) a small unfair gain
